answer: A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The basalt multiplier is published, charged in atlas, and ferrous lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 13 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A farm of 2561 identities would post 1422 proofs and burn roughly 12 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
